note: Codified from the City of Dripping Springs Code of Ordinances, Chapter 30 (Zoning and Development Code), Exhibit A, Section 3 (Zoning Districts) — Supplement 10, current 2026. Source is Municode; each district cites its own Section 3.x deep-link. MODELING NOTES: (1) The Dripping Springs code states only 'impervious coverage'/'impervious cover' per district and does NOT state a separate building lot-coverage cap, so max_impervious_pct is ordinance-sourced and max_lot_coverage_pct is flagged not_specified in provenance, carrying the impervious value as a conservative stand-in (the envelope draw uses setbacks, not this field). (2) SF-1 side yard is stated as 'Total of 40 feet combining both side yards with a minimum of 15 feet on either side' — the per-side minimum (15) is codified as side_ft; SF-1 states no distinct corner rule so side_corner_ft mirrors side_ft. (3) Distinct corner side yards are stated only for SF-3 (7.5) and SF-4 (15); other residential districts state no separate corner value so side_corner_ft mirrors side_ft. (4) For commercial districts (O/LR/GR/CS/I), side_ft is the base 'Minimum side yard' and side_corner_ft is the '__ feet adjacent to a public street or residential lot' figure. (5) Heights are 'two and one-half stories, or 40 feet' — the 40 ft cap is codified. P-258 LANE-C ADDENDUM (2026-09-16, acquisition campaign, branch seat/p258-lane-c): 9 districts added -- AG, O, LR, GR, CS, I, GUI, PP and MH -- from the same instrument this file already cites (Dripping Springs Code of Ordinances, Chapter 30 Zoning, Exhibit A Zoning Ordinance, Section 3 Zoning Districts, sections 3.2 and 3.9 through 3.18). HOW THEY WERE READ, BECAUSE IT MATTERS FOR THIS CITY: Municode's Dripping Springs pages render client-side and return only an empty Angular shell to a plain fetch -- this pass re-confirmed that (a direct fetch of the Section 3 deep link returned the app shell, zero table content). The section text WAS reached by loading the Municode page in a real browser session and reading the rendered Section 3 document, and every quote below is copied from that rendering. Any future re-verification needs the same browser-based route. ADDED VALUES: AG F50 / side not_specified / corner 25 / R50 / H40 / IC30; O F15 / S10 / corner 15 / R10 / H40 / IC60; LR F15 / S10 / corner 15 / R10 / H40 / IC60; GR F25 / S25 / corner 25 / R25 / H40 / IC60; CS F25 / S15 / corner 25 / R25 / H40 / IC70; I F60 / S15 / corner 50 / R25 / H40 / IC70; GUI F20 / S10 / corner not_specified (mirrors 10) / R20 / H40 / IC50; PP all yards 0 ('N/A') / H18 / IC3; MH F20 / S15 / corner not_specified (mirrors 15) / R20 / H20 / IC50. MAPPING RULES USED, BOTH ALREADY ESTABLISHED IN THIS FILE. (1) side_corner_ft for the O/LR/GR/CS/I commercial districts is the section's '__ feet adjacent to a public street or residential lot' figure, exactly as this file's original modelling note (4) prescribed; those sections also state 'all yards adjacent to a street shall be considered a front yard'. GUI and MH state no street-side figure at all, so their side_corner_ft mirrors the side minimum and is flagged not_specified (0.7) rather than asserted, matching note (3)'s treatment of the residential rows. (2) max_lot_coverage_pct is not_specified on every added row with the section's impervious figure as the stand-in, because Dripping Springs states impervious coverage only -- the same convention the existing SF/MF rows use. TWO DELIBERATE NON-SUBSTITUTIONS. (1) AG's side yard is 'Ten percent of the lot width, not to exceed 30 feet', i.e. a computed percentage, so AG's side_ft is not_specified (100 sentinel) and NO scalar was invented -- the 30 ft. ceiling is a cap on a computed value and is not a side yard. Its corner value (25 ft. from a street right-of-way) IS in feet and is codified. (2) PP's impervious cover of THREE PERCENT is transcribed verbatim from Section 3.16.5(c): it is an extraordinarily low cap and is very likely a drafting artifact in the adopted text, but the campaign's rule is to quote what the code says rather than to correct it, so it is quoted and flagged here for a reviewer. WHY THESE NINE WERE MISSING BEFORE: the original note here recorded the commercial districts' mapping rule (side = base minimum, corner = the street/residential figure) while rowing only the six residential districts, so the rule was known but the rows were never written. That gap is now closed for every lane-c code in this city except PR (Public Recreation, not a lane-c code). VERIFICATION STATE AND atom_did, STATED PLAINLY: these rows carry verification_state 'primary-source-verified' (read and quoted from the live primary source this pass) and deliberately carry NO atom_did. This pass could not round-trip the text against the code-section atom corpus, and this corpus has an explicit history of a fabricated atom_did (see kyle-tx.json's note); asserting an atom id that was not round-tripped would repeat that defect. If the atoms exist for 3.2 and 3.9-3.18, a later pass should add the atom_did and promote these rows to human-verified. SOURCES TRIED: Municode (READ via browser session -- source of every value); a plain automated fetch of the same Municode URL (returned the Angular shell, no content); the file's own pre-existing citation set (carried). eCode360, American Legal, the city document centre and ArcGIS REST were not tried for this city because the Municode publication served the code once rendered.
